title: Finite type kernels into coherent restrictions on an open slice
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and $U\subseteq X$ an open. Let $\mathcal G$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $\mathcal F$ a finite type $\mathcal O_U$-module [pqf-def-coherent], where $\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_X|_U$ and sheaves of modules are as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For any morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G|_U$, its kernel is of finite type on $U$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BY (lemma-coherent-abelian), part (2), applied on the open ringed space; Definition 01BV (definition-coherent)

proof.text: The open slice has objects the opens V of X contained in U, with the same rings, restrictions and covering families. These are the opens of the open ringed space U. The induced identification of module categories preserves finite free sheaves, epimorphisms, kernels and local generating data, since all are defined by these same rings, maps and coverings. G restricted to U is coherent: restrict its local generators to intersections with U; a finite free map over any V contained in U has finite type kernel by the relation clause for G on X.

Under this identification apply part (2) of the finite type submodule and kernel lemma on the ringed space U to F -> G restricted to U. For completeness, near each point choose a finite free epimorphism P -> F. Its composite into G has finite type kernel L by coherence. Local lifts of sections killed by phi lie in L, so L maps epimorphically to kernel phi. Its image is finite type. These neighborhoods cover U, proving the claimed finite type condition; transport the local generators back to the slice.
